== THIS RECORD DOES NOT UNBLOCK THE PR -- READ THIS BEFORE EXPECTING GREEN ==

reviews/70/cloud-reviewer-b.json is a DISAGREE at 5fa8e75, a commit the branch has since superseded. I expected my AGREE to satisfy the gate beside it. IT DOES NOT, and I verified that by running the gate with this very record staged rather than by predicting it:

  python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr 70
  -> still FAILS: "reviews/70/cloud-reviewer-b.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'"

I then isolated the cause, to prove the blocker is B's verdict and not a defect in MY record: with reviews/70/cloud-reviewer-b.json temporarily moved aside in my local worktree ONLY, and my record the sole record present, the same command printed "lwb-lanes check passed" and exited 0. So this record is provably well-formed, schema-valid, identity-independent (no shared segment at or above the 8-character floor), and fresh against the reviewable head -- it satisfies REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS on its own. I restored B's file immediately; that experiment was local and reverted, and I have NOT removed, edited or in any way altered B's record on the branch.

This is DELIBERATE, not a bug. In scripts/lwb_lanes.py, _review_ok checks `verdict != "AGREE"` at ~line 741 and tags the rejection "other"; the STALENESS check sits LATER, at ~line 771. So a DISAGREE is classified as dissent BEFORE anyone asks whether it reviewed a commit that still exists. independent_reviews then routes "other" rejections straight into the caller's errors UNCONDITIONALLY and forces its own return to False -- its docstring says so in terms: "dissent and identity problems... must never be outvoted by an unrelated valid record." Only STALE-and-only-STALE rejections are downgradable churn.

The consequence: once any reviewer files a DISAGREE, no later AGREE at any head can clear lwb-lanes on that PR, because the DISAGREE is judged on its verdict before its staleness is ever considered. That is why PR #46's title is "drop two unclearable stale DISAGREE records" and why #53 and #66 exist as re-cuts. The repo's own history shows the only route taken so far is to re-cut the branch.

I will NOT delete or edit reviewer B's record. It is another reviewer's dissent and an audit-trail artifact; removing it to make a gate pass is exactly the falsification this role exists to prevent, and my authorisation is to add a record, not to curate the directory. My AGREE stands as the independent verdict on the current head; clearing B's superseded DISAGREE is an author/owner decision, and the two options visible from here are a re-cut branch (the precedent) or a deliberate change to lwb_lanes.py so that a DISAGREE which is ALSO stale is treated as superseded churn -- which is a design decision with real risk (it would let dissent be aged out by pushing commits) and is emphatically not mine to make unilaterally.

== A SEPARATE, PRE-EXISTING HAZARD ON MAIN, NOT THIS PR'S ==

`python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` FAILS at this head: "proof/39.json: python3 scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check: digest mismatch -- recorded sha256 'ab8f5e3b...', re-run 'ded08fb2...'".

I did NOT charge this to the PR. I checked out UNTOUCHED origin/main (0d1be714) in a separate worktree and ran the same command: it fails there too, identically, on the same proof/39.json command (re-run digest '47522473...'). The mismatch is PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN; this PR only changes which wrong digest is reported, because HANDOFF.md's byte count differs. Cause: proof/39.json recorded a digest of lwb_handoff.py --check output, whose text embeds HANDOFF.md's byte size, so any later HANDOFF edit invalidates it.

Harmless today, NOT harmless soon, and this is the one thing in this review I would want an owner to see: ci.yml's lwb-proof-reexecute step is `continue-on-error: true`, explicitly "REPORT-ONLY, deliberately... can never fail the job". PR #62 ("Make lwb-proof-reexecute blocking") flips exactly that -- I read its diff: `- continue-on-error: true` and the step renamed from "report-only" to "blocking". If #62 lands while proof/39.json's digest is stale on main, MAIN GOES RED, and it is red for every subsequent PR until re-recorded. Recommend re-recording proof/39.json's handoff digest, or marking that command non-verifiable, BEFORE #62 merges. Filed here rather than as a comment on #62 to keep reviewer noise down; #62 already carries a current AGREE and this is a merge-ORDER decision, not a defect in #62's diff.

== TRIAGE NOTE: A FALSE-ACCUSATION TRAP IN MY OWN DISPATCH INSTRUCTIONS ==

My instructions say to skip a PR whose reviews/<pr>/ holds a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA, and to review EVERY unreviewed open PR. Applied literally, all 14 open PRs look unreviewed, because committing a record advances the raw head past the sha that record names. The gate does not compare against the raw head: resolve_reviewable_head skips commits touching only reviews/ and proof/. Comparing against the REVIEWABLE head instead, 13 of 14 open PRs (45, 46, 51, 53, 58, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 66, 68, 69) already carry a CURRENT AGREE record naming their reviewable head, and only #70 genuinely lacked one. Had I followed the instruction as written I would have filed 13 redundant records naming shas the gate never compares against -- each of which would have been stale the instant I pushed it, since my own commit moves the raw head. Recording it so the next run need not rediscover it; reviewer B's #70 record and reviewer A's #69 record reach the same conclusion independently, which is now three independent derivations of the same correction.

Caveat on that triage, stated because it is a real limit: I replicated resolve_reviewable_head with `git log --format=%H <head>`, matching main's CURRENT all-parents walk. PR #63 changes that walk to --first-parent. My triage would differ from a post-#63 gate on any branch containing a merge whose side history holds non-record commits. It does not affect #70, which has no merge commits and whose reviewable head equals its raw head (9700513, 0 commits skipped).
